rooms.prompt:
Walk the robot to the exit.
a0 holds the robot's address. An int is 4 bytes, so each step right adds 4.
rooms.hint: Press → (or click the next cell) four times.

rooms.prompt:
Load arr[3] into a2, then reach the exit.
Base + offset: lw a2, 8(a0) loads the int 8 bytes past a0.
rooms.hint: Click arr[3] and load it: from 0x4000 it's 3 ints × 4 bytes = 12 bytes on.
rooms.explanation: R[rd] = M[R[rs1] + offset]: from a0 = 0x4000, lw a2, 12(a0) reads 0x400C, which is arr[3] = 40. (The slides write it lw x12, 12(x10).) After one step, the same int is lw a2, 8(a0).

rooms.prompt:
Store 8 in arr[3] to open its door, then reach the exit.
sw writes a register into memory, and t2 holds 8.
rooms.hint: Click arr[3] and store t2 there: sw t2, 12(a0) from where you start.
rooms.explanation: M[R[rs1] + offset] = R[rs2]: sw t2, 12(a0) writes 8 over the 40 at 0x400C (the slides' sw x7, 12(x10)), so the array is now 5, 90, 100, 8, 11.

rooms.prompt:
Reach the exit with at most 3 instructions.
It's too far to walk, so teach the robot one step and let it repeat.
rooms.hint: loop:, then one step right, then Repeat while a0 ≠ a1.
rooms.explanation: bne a0, a1, loop jumps back to loop: until a0 equals a1: one step written, seven steps taken.

rooms.prompt:
Reach the exit, two rows down.
Rows sit end to end in memory. This room is 4 words wide, so one row down is 16 bytes on.
rooms.hint: Go down twice (+16 each), then right three times.
rooms.explanation: Memory is one long line of bytes: the word below is a whole row later, so a step down is addi a0, a0, 16 here. Any word is at base + 4 × (row × width + column).

rooms.prompt:
Open the door, then reach the exit.
The door holds 7 and opens at 12. Memory can't do math: load it, add 5 in a register, store it back.
rooms.hint: Load the door into t0, press addi t0, t0, 5, then store t0 back into the door.
rooms.explanation: RISC-V is a load/store architecture: data is loaded into registers, processed there, and written back with stores. lw, addi, sw is how door = door + 5 really runs.

rooms.prompt:
Swap the two doors' words, then reach the exit.
Each door holds the code the other one needs. You have two registers, t0 and t1.
rooms.code_snippet: t = A; A = B; B = t;
rooms.hint: Load both doors first (into t0 and t1), then store each register into the other door.
rooms.explanation: A swap needs two registers: load both words before storing, or the first store overwrites a value you still need. Negative offsets reach backwards: door A is above and behind the robot.

rooms.prompt:
Fill the blanks so t0 = arr[i] + arr[i+1].
It's tested with i = 1 and i = 3, so it has to work for any i.
rooms.code_snippet: sum = arr[i] + arr[i+1];   // arr is t1, i is t2, sum is t0
rooms.hint: arr[i] is at arr + i × 4 (slli by 2), and arr[i+1] is one int, 4 bytes, after it.
rooms.explanation: Find the address once: t3 = t1 + (i << 2) is &arr[i]. Then arr[i] is 0(t3) and arr[i+1] is 4(t3).

rooms.prompt:
Fill the blanks to finish this if/else.
x is a0 and y is a1. It's tested with x = 3 and x = 7, so both paths have to work.
rooms.code_snippet: if (x < 5) y = y + 3; else y = y << 1;
rooms.hint: slti sets t0 to 1 when x < 5. Branch to else when t0 is 0, and make the if part jump over else.
rooms.explanation: beq t0, x0, else skips the if part when x ≥ 5 (y: 4 → 8). With x = 3, y becomes 7 and j done jumps over else; without it, the if part falls into else and doubles y too.

rooms.prompt:
Reach the exit: the first 0 in this row.
Teach a loop that stops when it loads a 0 (x0 always holds 0).
rooms.hint: Step, load the new word into t1, then Repeat while t1 ≠ 0.
rooms.explanation: A sentinel loop stops on the data, not on a count: bne t1, x0, loop goes round again while the word just loaded isn't 0.

rooms.prompt:
Copy a[] into the vault below it, then reach the exit.
Teach the robot one int, then Repeat. This room is 7 words wide.
rooms.hint: Tap loop:, load the int under you, store it 28 bytes on (a row down), step right. Then Repeat while a0 < a1.
rooms.explanation: Everything in the loop is relative to a0, so the same four lines copy every int: lw, sw 28(a0), step 4, and blt back while a0 < a1. bge would jump back only once a0 ≥ a1.

rooms.prompt:
Add values[0] through values[5] into t2, then reach the exit.
The loop from lecture: t0 is i, and t6 holds 6.
rooms.hint: Tap loop:, load values[i] into t1, add it to t2, step, add 1 to i, then Repeat while i < 6.
rooms.explanation: Load values[i], add it to the sum, move to the next int, and i++: blt t0, t6 jumps back while i < 6. The lecture finds values[i] with slli t1, t0, 2 (i × 4); stepping a0 by 4 each pass does the same job.

rooms.prompt:
Fill the blanks so the loop adds 2 to every int in arr.
i is t0 and counts down from 3. The tests check arr and where i ends up.
rooms.hint: Store the new value back where you loaded it from, and keep looping while i ≥ 0.
rooms.explanation: The body runs 4 times (i = 3, 2, 1, 0): arr becomes 5, 7, 9, 11 and t0 ends at -1. bne t0, x0 would stop before i = 0 and skip arr[0].

rooms.prompt:
Fill the blanks so main finishes with a0 = 10.
main calls func, then adds 1. jal puts PC + 4 in ra and jumps; jalr jumps back to ra.
rooms.hint: jal ra, func at 0x104 sets ra = 0x108. func returns with jalr x0, 0(ra).
rooms.explanation: jal ra, func at 0x104 saves 0x108 (PC + 4) in ra and jumps to func; jalr x0, 0(ra) jumps back to 0x108, which adds the 1. j func jumps without saving a return address, and 4(ra) would skip the add.

rooms.prompt:
Fill the blanks so main stores func(6) in result and returns.
main saves ra and a0 on the stack before the call and restores both before returning.
rooms.hint: Make room with addi sp, sp, -8, save ra at 4(sp) before jal overwrites it, and store func's answer before lw a0, 0(sp) brings back main's old a0.
rooms.explanation: main allocates 8 bytes (addi sp, sp, -8). jal ra, func overwrites ra with 0x114, which is why main saved its own return address first. func returns 9 in a0, but lw a0, 0(sp) brings back main's old a0 (2), so the answer has to be stored before that.

rooms.prompt:
Copy a[] into the vault before the Chip Chomper eats it.
The Chomper eats one int every 4 instructions, so keep the loop short.
rooms.hint: Tap loop:, then keep the loop to 4 instructions: load, store a row up (-28), step, Repeat. Every extra line slows every pass.
rooms.explanation: A loop costs its body times its passes: 4 instructions an int kept you just ahead of the Chomper's 4 instructions an int.
